Basel defender Victory Akpe has expressed his delight at captaining the Olympic Eagles to a commanding victory over the Democratic Republic of Congo, which secured Nigeria’s place in the final qualifying round of next year’s U-23 Africa Cup of Nations, PUNCH Sports Extra reports. The Olympic Eagles overturned a first-leg deficit with a convincing 4-0 win over DR Congo at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo, four days after losing the first leg in Lubumbashi. Akpe led the side as Alex Oweilayefa, Peter Osayande, Victor Samuel and Abdulmuiz Adeleke all got on the scoresheet to complete the comeback. The 20-year-old had been called up to the senior national team during the September international break but was withdrawn from the squad before being handed the responsibility of captaining the Olympic Eagles. “Great feeling to represent this country and put on that amazing jersey,” Akpe told PUNCH Sports Extra. U-23 goalie Atata reflects on Congo heroics U-23 AFCON: Olympic Eagles crush DR Congo 4-0, face Zambia Olympic Eagles chase comeback against DR Congo in Ikenne Reflecting on the pressure to overturn the first-leg defeat, the defender said the team needed time to build an understanding, having had little opportunity to play together before the tie. “Most of us played together for the first time, so we needed at least one game to understand one another. When we came back, we decided to learn fast from our mistakes and improve as fast as possible so we can play better than the first leg,” he said. At club level, Akpe has scored one goal and provided one assist in 13 league appearances for Basel this season. Nigeria will face Zambia in the final qualifying round for next year’s U-23 Africa Cup of Nations in Egypt. The tournament will determine Africa’s representatives in the men’s football event at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
